title: Seifert smoothing and Seifert circles of an oriented diagram
statement: Let $D$ be an oriented link diagram on $S^2$. At every crossing replace the two crossing arcs by the two non-crossing arcs that preserve the orientations (the Seifert smoothing); the result is a finite disjoint union of oriented simple closed curves in $S^2$, the **Seifert circles** of $D$, and the smoothed picture together with one signed short arc at each former crossing (the sign of the crossing) is the **Seifert picture** of $D$. No smoothing changes the number of components; the signed arcs join distinct Seifert circles (or a circle to itself) and lie in the complement of the circles.
strategy: Seifert's algorithm as used by the Yamada-Vogel method; the orientation-respecting smoothing is fixed once and for all, and the signed arcs record the crossings that were smoothed.

references.title: Birman and Brendle, Braids: A Survey, Handbook of Knot Theory chapter, author manuscript; section 2 (printed pp. 12-26) and Figures 3-12
Traczyk, A new proof of Markov's braid theorem, Banach Center Publications 42 (1998), 409-419
